summary: Peloton's workouts list endpoint (GET /api/user/{user_id}/workouts) nests ride/class metadata under a "ride" object (ride.title, ride.id) rather than flattening it to the top level -- confirmed live against a real account (2026-08-13). The typed workouts table's column extraction (lookupFieldValue(obj, "title")/"ride_id") only ever looks at the top level, and the endpoint requires a joins=ride query param to include the nested object at all (the single-fetch `workouts list` command already defaults this via its own --joins flag; sync's flat loop builds its own params independently and did not). Any future regen must keep both: sync sending joins=ride for the "workouts" resource, and enrichWorkoutRideMetadata (store/peloton.go) promoting ride.title/ride.id to the top level before typed-column extraction and raw JSON storage -- dropping either one reintroduces null title/ride_id on synced workouts.
reason: Synced workouts had null title and ride_id despite the API actually returning the data (confirmed via direct sqlite3 inspection of a live sync), because sync never requested the joins and, independently, the generic top-level-only field extraction can't see data Peloton nests under "ride" even when the API does return it.
validated_outcome: Verified live: a scoped sync of 100 real workouts populated title (e.g. "5 min Post-Run Stretch", "45 min Power Zone Endurance Ride") and ride_id for all re-synced rows. Full go build/vet/test suite passes.
